summary: CapSense on the QWA309 PSoC 4000T (EZI2C @0x08, SCB5): auto-detects the SDK 3-byte frame [btn0][btn1][slider] or the raw5 data block (5-segment slider raw counts, own baseline, centroid 0..100)
guideline: TESAIoT SDK (guideline only, never built): bento-firmware-template-mtb-only/bento_libs/claw/common/capsense/src/i2c_driver/capsense_i2c.c + api/capsense_protocol.h (ASCII or numeric bytes; baseline)
hw_settings: QWA309 CS select switch = ON (enables the base-board I2C; else buttons/CapSense are dead)
notes: raw5: thresholds 350/200 counts on own baseline (idle noise +-30, touch 1500..5000, neighbours rise ~250); the block's own baseline words are not used (that firmware drags its baseline down during a touch). Do not touch the pads during init. The SDK reads CapSense from the CM55 that owns SCB5 - here i2c-scb5 (CM33_NS) owns SCB5, one owner core per app
verified: 2026-10-10 second tesaiot board (4000T with raw5 firmware), app qwa309-io: format auto-detected at boot (retry after E84 reset), slide left->right 0..100 in order, taps left/middle/right -> pos 0 / 47-50 / 100 with clean touch/release; raw5 firmware scans no buttons. frame3 path unverified (no board with that firmware). Our first board: 4000T never ACKs 0x08.
